solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sole trader?

blocks.note: surface reading: a one-person business, a sole trader in the legal sense
setter's reading: someone who trades in sole, the flatfish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole trader' is a business term for a self-employed person; read with sole as the fish, it is someone selling fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishmonger is a retailer of fish, and sole is one of the fish on the slab.

clue.text: Confront female pilot who's downed a few

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
a fighter ace is a pilot credited with shooting down several enemy aircraft

explanation.surface: A woman flyer squares up to someone, perhaps after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downed a few' suggests drinking, but it means shooting down enemy planes.
explanation.definitionFit: To face a problem or person is to confront it head on; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Band of elite soldiers on horse

blocks.note: the Special Air Service, the British army's elite special forces regiment
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A group of crack troops is mounted on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is drug slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: Undocking for the first time when playing any video game

indicators.note: playing with something moves its parts around, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gamer sees a ship leave port for the first time in whatever video game is on.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's maiden voyage is its first trip, the first time it leaves the dock.

clue.text: Simone grapples with Jack, a martial art expert

indicators.note: a wrestler who grapples wraps arms around an opponent, so one name encloses the other

blocks.note: Nina Simone, the American jazz and soul singer
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A woman called Simone wrestles a man called Jack, who knows martial arts.
explanation.walkthrough: Simone is a surname here: the first name of singer Nina Simone is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja is a Japanese warrior trained in ninjutsu, a covert martial art.

clue.text: Reportedly, setter invents enhancement for viewers

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how it is spoken

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself as I
to make up a story is to invent it

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler is said to have invented something to improve eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter is 'I' or 'me'; 'I make up' and EYE MAKE-UP are said the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes are viewers in the sense of the organs that see, and cosmetics like mascara enhance them.

clue.text: Skip over technical college

blocks.note: O is the scorecard abbreviation for an over in cricket
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone decides to bypass a technical college.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, which is what skipping it does.

clue.text: First of many different odd bits of trouble she's expecting

indicators.note: the first of a word means only its opening character is kept
odd bits are the characters in the first, third, fifth and seventh places

blocks.note: opening letter of many
other means different, as in 'some other time'
first, third, fifth and seventh letters of trouble

explanation.surface: A woman with all sorts of problems is pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnant woman is said to be expecting, and a mother-to-be is just that.

clue.text: Hollywood won't listen, unfortunately

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters come out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Sadly, the film industry refuses to hear criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinseltown is a nickname for Hollywood, mocking its glittery but shallow glamour.

clue.text: Major supplier of beluga canapés is a rogue

indicators.note: a rogue element behaves unpredictably, so the letters break out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written, accent dropped

explanation.surface: A canapé topped with beluga caviar has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: Beluga is the sturgeon whose roe is the costliest caviar, not the white whale.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest inland water body and the main source of beluga sturgeon and their caviar.

clue.text: Leader from Times in "wrong paper" shock!

indicators.note: a leader is what goes at the front, so only the opening character is used
placed in means put inside the other piece

blocks.note: for a Times solver, the Sun tabloid is the wrong newspaper
opening letter of Times

explanation.surface: A Times editorial appears in a rival newspaper, to general amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid owned by the same company as The Times; the setter calls it the wrong paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or astonish them so they cannot react.

clue.text: Instruction to leave hotel room?

blocks.note: surface reading: a demand that a guest check out of the room
setter's reading: a sign telling staff to leave the room alone, to let it be

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like 'depart from', but here it means 'leave alone', as the sign on the door handle asks.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the wording of the hanging card that tells hotel staff not to enter.

clue.text: A colourful compound wager at one race worked out

indicators.note: something worked out has been processed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a wager is a bet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A punter places an elaborate combination bet on a single race.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound looks like a betting term, an accumulator bet, but it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta carotene is the orange pigment in carrots, a chemical compound that gives colour.

clue.text: Breaks, going green

blocks.note: surface reading: something snapping and turning green, like mouldy or rotting matter
setter's reading: holidays taken in an environmentally friendly way

explanation.walkthrough: Breaks are holidays and 'going green' is adopting environmental values.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecotourism is travel to natural areas planned to limit harm to the environment, so holidays with a green conscience.

clue.text: Plane's small thrusts to experience

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
pokes are short jabs or thrusts
to have a good time is to experience one

explanation.surface: An aircraft makes little pushes forward to gain experience.
explanation.walkthrough: Plane is the carpentry tool, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokeshave is a small two-handled woodworking plane, used for shaping curved pieces such as wheel spokes.

clue.text: National team member always departs eastern archipelago

blocks.note: a player picked for a national side wins a cap, and is called a cap
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A player for the national side keeps leaving for a chain of islands in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Verde is an island nation, a group of volcanic islands off West Africa in the Atlantic.

clue.text: Kart (e-vehicle) overturned rounding entrance to cambered circuit

indicators.note: a vehicle overturned is upside down, so in a down clue the run of letters is flipped end to end
the entrance to a word is where it begins, its opening character
going round something means surrounding it, so the flipped run is put around the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letter E
a car is a vehicle
opening letter of cambered

explanation.surface: An electric go-kart flips over while taking a banked bend on a track.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis splits as e + vehicle; the reversal of those three pieces then wraps round the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A racetrack is a circuit, a closed course on which races are run.

clue.text: Firm taken aback by name of offensive group

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: CO is short for company, a firm
the Tet Offensive of 1968 in the Vietnam War

explanation.surface: A company is shocked by the name of a rude band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like an adjective meaning rude, but it is a military campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, typically musicians playing together.

clue.text: Wine temperature fine

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
okay means fine, all right

explanation.surface: The wine is at the right temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet dessert wine from the Tokaj region of Hungary.

clue.text: These gorgeous lips which might be to blame for a broken heart?

definitions.text: These gorgeous lips which might be to blame for a broken heart?

blocks.note: first reading: the double curve of a shapely upper lip

blocks.clueFragment: might be to blame for a broken heart?
blocks.note: second reading: the weapon of the Roman love god, whose arrows pierce hearts

explanation.walkthrough: The upper lip's curve is named after the bow of the god of love, whose arrow is what wounds a heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid's bow is the name for the double-curved line of the upper lip, shaped like an archer's bow.

clue.text: Least attractive suit lengths I tailored

indicators.note: a tailored garment is cut and resewn into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tailor makes the ugliest suit from the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsightly means ugly to look at, so the superlative is least attractive.

clue.text: Home terminal initially loaded with back up data

indicators.note: initially points to the first character of the word before it
going back means travelling the other way, so the short word is read from its end
something loaded with cargo carries it inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: being in means being at home
opening letter of terminal
the word up read backwards

explanation.surface: A home computer terminal is loaded up with backup data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back up' looks like a computing term, but back is the reversal signal and up the word reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is the information fed into a computer, so it serves as a noun for data.

clue.text: Flipping keen prima donna!

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word is read from the other end

blocks.note: avid means keen or eager

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about an over-eager leading lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive, but it is the signal to turn the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna is the leading female opera singer, also called a diva; both words also describe a temperamental star.

clue.text: Declined to fire whistleblower taken advantage of

indicators.note: firing someone gets rid of them, so that part is dismissed from the word

blocks.note: to decline an offer is to refuse it
a referee blows a whistle in football and is called the ref

explanation.surface: A company refused to sack a whistleblower and so exploited them.
explanation.walkthrough: A whistleblower suggests someone exposing wrongdoing; here it is the match official with the whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: To be used is to be exploited, taken advantage of by someone.

clue.text: Goodness regularly exhibited by Miss Mary?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other character is shown

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of Miss Mary

explanation.surface: Is Miss Mary a model of virtue?
explanation.walkthrough: I say! is an old-fashioned British exclamation of surprise, like Goodness!
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, so the interjection goodness stands for the phrase.

clue.text: They cover some guitar Paul insured

indicators.note: some means a part of what follows, so the letters sit within a run of words

blocks.note: runs from the end of guitar through Paul into the start of insured

explanation.surface: A musician called Paul has had some of his guitars insured.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpaulins are heavy waterproof sheets used to cover things, so they are things that cover.

clue.text: Look chaps! India's opener's caught

indicators.note: an opener is what comes first, so only the opening character is kept
something caught is held inside, so one piece is trapped by the other

blocks.note: chaps are men
opening letter of India

explanation.surface: A cricket fan shouts that India's opening batsman has been caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket: an opener is the first batsman, but here it is just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or bearing, their appearance and manner.

clue.text: Small shrew reportedly tunnelled into rolling transporter

indicators.note: reported words are passed on by speech, so what matters is the sound

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
Kate is the title character of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
to bore is to tunnel, and the past tense sounds like a plank

explanation.surface: A tiny shrew is said to have burrowed into a wheeled carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: The shrew is not the small mammal but the shrewish heroine of Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A skateboard is a board on wheels that carries its rider along, a transporter that rolls.
